title: Model Stock: All We Need Is Just a Few Fine-Tuned Models
what_it_is: Layer-wise merge of N fine-tuned models toward the pretrained weights, with the interpolation ratio t = N cos(theta)/(1+(N-1)cos(theta)) set by the angle between fine-tuned weights; no extra training. Abstract + method read: with 2 CLIP fine-tunes it beats Model Soup on ImageNet and 5 OOD sets.
why_it_could_help_us: We already hold 5 seeds per config (PF, C2 HRNet-W18+SWAD) from one ImageNet init; merging them post hoc gives one deployable model that may carry part of the 5-member PF ensemble gain (E1 inactive +0.21 PASS, crack +0.035 n.d.) at single-model cost and D4 TTA unchanged.
cost_to_try: config-only (post-hoc weight merge + BN stat recompute)
risk_or_reason_against: Evidence is CLIP ViT classification only; our models are CNNs with BatchNorm and a decoder trained from scratch (decoder has no pretrained anchor, so use plain average there); PF freezes the encoder for 1k steps, which may make seeds very close (angle small, little gain).

title: Lookaround Optimizer: k steps around, 1 step average
what_it_is: Optimizer that trains k copies from a common point, each on a different data augmentation, then averages them every few steps; full text sections read: CIFAR and ImageNet, CNNs and ViTs, from scratch and fine-tuning.
why_it_could_help_us: Around-step augmentations can be the 8 D4 transforms we already use at test time, so the averaged weights are pushed toward D4-consistent flat minima; SWAD can still average the Lookaround trajectory.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (training loop; k x compute per step, fits 8 GPUs)
risk_or_reason_against: No dense-prediction evidence; k-fold compute; gain over SWAD (which already flattens) is unknown.

title: Ensemble of Averages: Improving Model Selection and Boosting Performance in Domain Generalization
what_it_is: Ensemble of moving-average (SWA/EMA) models from independent runs; abstract: DomainBed RN50 68.0% vs ERM about 64%, RegNetY-16GF 76.6%; averaging also improves in-domain/out-domain rank correlation for model selection.
why_it_could_help_us: Our 5-seed ensembles (PF2E) were plain models; an ensemble of 5 C2 SWAD models is the EoA recipe and needs no new training. The rank-correlation result is relevant to our noisy CV-to-E1 selection.
risk_or_reason_against: Deployment cost x5; PF ensemble gain on E1 crack was n.d. and SKR2E failed a guard; may only re-measure a known ensemble effect.

title: Model Ratatouille: Recycling Diverse Models for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
what_it_is: Fine-tune the same pretrained model on several auxiliary tasks, use each as init for a target fine-tune, then average all target fine-tunes; abstract: new SOTA on DomainBed.
why_it_could_help_us: We have auxiliary labelled crack/defect sets (E-SCDD, UCF-EL, pavement crack sets): auxiliary fine-tunes of the HRNet-W18 encoder on them give diverse inits whose averaged target models may generalise better to unseen modules than seed-only diversity.
cost_to_try: new pipeline (aux fine-tunes + target fine-tunes + average)
risk_or_reason_against: Head shapes differ across tasks (reinit heads); averaging needs all runs to stay in one basin; classification-only evidence.

title: IMWA: Iterative Model Weight Averaging benefits class-imbalanced learning
what_it_is: Iterative averaging of parallel models in episodes; abstract (preview): model weight averaging helps class-imbalanced learning, with early-epoch averaging.
why_it_could_help_us: Crack (0.19% of pixels) and inactive (42/478 cells) are rare classes; IMWA argues WA gains are largest exactly there.

title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
what_it_is: Uniform or greedy averaging of models fine-tuned from one init with different hyperparameters.
why_it_could_help_us: Baseline for Model Stock on our 5 seeds; greedy soup can be selected on CV folds only.

title: Diverse Weight Averaging for Out-of-Distribution Generalization
what_it_is: Average weights of runs with diverse hyperparameters from a shared init.
why_it_could_help_us: Same as soups; diversity from hyperparameter sweeps we may already have.

title: Robust fine-tuning of zero-shot models (WiSE-FT)
what_it_is: Interpolate fine-tuned and pretrained weights.
why_it_could_help_us: Encoder-only WiSE between ImageNet HRNet-W18 and the C2 encoder is a one-parameter sweep.
risk_or_reason_against: Already in MASTER (RUN_AFTER_GATE); decoder has no pretrained point.

title: Exponential Moving Average of Weights in Deep Learning: Dynamics and Benefits
what_it_is: Systematic study of EMA of weights.
why_it_could_help_us: Post-hoc EMA was already tested; listed for completeness.
risk_or_reason_against: Already in MASTER and tested (post-hoc EMA).

what_it_is: Checkpoint averaging along the trajectory with high learning rates speeds convergence in LLM pretraining (abstract preview).

title: Stochastic Weight Averaging Revisited

why_it_could_help_us: Background for SWAD window choice.

why_it_could_help_us: Medical-domain WA evidence under scanner shift, analogous to our source shift.

title: Continual test-time adaptation via weight averaging of feature augmentations in cross-domain medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Weight averaging used in continual test-time adaptation for cross-domain medical segmentation (title only; no abstract in index).
why_it_could_help_us: If E1-like new modules arrive in batches, WA-based TTA could adapt BN/weights per module.
risk_or_reason_against: No abstract reachable; TTA was covered by D31.

title: Branch Soup: Improving vision foundation models via averaging adapter weights of branched checkpoints
what_it_is: Average adapter weights of checkpoints branched from one fine-tune (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Cheap soup variant: branch from the C2 checkpoint at step 10k with different seeds/augment, average.
risk_or_reason_against: VFM adapters, not CNN full fine-tune.

title: SWAD: Domain Generalization by Seeking Flat Minima
what_it_is: Dense stochastic weight averaging; in use in C2.
why_it_could_help_us: Reference point for every row in this family.

title: Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Efficiently Improving Generalization
what_it_is: SAM optimizer.
why_it_could_help_us: Never run although RUN_NOW in MASTER; FAD Table 1 (read) shows SAM +0.8 pp over Adam on DG benchmarks.

title: ASAM: Adaptive Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Scale-Invariant Learning of Deep Neural Networks
what_it_is: SAM with a perturbation radius normalised by weight scale, so sharpness is invariant to parameter rescaling (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Our CNN has BatchNorm, where plain SAM's fixed radius is scale-sensitive; ASAM is the safer SAM variant to run if P142 is run.
risk_or_reason_against: Classification evidence; flatness gain may overlap with SWAD.

title: Surrogate Gap Minimization Improves Sharpness-Aware Training (GSAM)
what_it_is: SAM variant that also minimises the gap between perturbed and clean loss (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Alternative SAM variant.
risk_or_reason_against: Mostly ViT classification; one more hyperparameter.

title: Gradient Norm Aware Minimization Seeks First-Order Flatness and Improves Generalization (GAM)
what_it_is: Optimizer penalising first-order flatness (max gradient norm in a neighbourhood) (abstract preview); FAD Table 1: GAM 66.6 vs SAM 66.4 avg on DG sets.
why_it_could_help_us: Same use as SAM.

title: Flatness-Aware Minimization for Domain Generalization (FAD)
what_it_is: Optimizer combining zeroth- and first-order flatness; full text read: average over PACS/VLCS/OfficeHome/TerraInc/DomainNet/NICO++ 67.6 vs GAM 66.6, SAM 66.4, AdamW 66.0, Adam 65.6 (ResNet-50, DomainBed protocol).
why_it_could_help_us: Directly built for unseen-domain generalisation (our unseen modules / CSIR shift); the paper also tests optimizers combined with SWAD (Section 4.3).
cost_to_try: config-only (optimizer swap, about 2 to 3x step cost)
risk_or_reason_against: I did not read the SWAD-combination table; the text says AdamW was best among base optimizers with SWAD, so FAD+SWAD may not beat AdamW+SWAD. Classification only.

title: Seeking Consistent Flat Minima for Better Domain Generalization via Refining Loss Landscapes
what_it_is: Refines loss landscapes so flat minima are consistent across domains (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Our five sources are natural domains; a source-consistent flatness objective targets the unseen-source failure.
risk_or_reason_against: Classification DG; method details not read.

title: Friendly Sharpness-Aware Minimization
what_it_is: Analyses which part of the SAM perturbation helps and proposes F-SAM (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Cheaper/stabler SAM variant to try if SAM helps.

title: Towards Efficient and Scalable Sharpness-Aware Minimization (LookSAM)
what_it_is: Computes the SAM ascent step only periodically to cut the 2x cost (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Halves SAM cost if flatness optimizers are screened at 2 seeds x 5 folds.

title: A Retinal Vessel Segmentation Method Based on the Sharpness-Aware Minimization Model
what_it_is: Adds SAM to RF-UNet on DRIVE; abstract: better validation loss, accuracy, sensitivity, F1, AUC.
why_it_could_help_us: Only thin-structure segmentation evidence for SAM found; supports running P142 on cracks.
risk_or_reason_against: Single small dataset (DRIVE 20/20), low-tier venue, no seed statistics in abstract.

title: Sharpness-Aware Gradient Matching for Domain Generalization (SAGM)
what_it_is: SAM variant aligning clean and perturbed gradients for DG.
why_it_could_help_us: DG-specific SAM.

title: Fisher SAM: Information Geometry and Sharpness Aware Minimisation
what_it_is: SAM with Fisher-metric neighbourhood (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Variant only.

title: A Modern Look at the Relationship between Sharpness and Generalization
what_it_is: Study showing sharpness does not reliably correlate with generalisation across settings (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Caution: flatness measures may not predict our E1 gains; argues for testing, not assuming.

title: Domain Generalization by Mutual-Information Regularization with Pre-trained Models (MIRO)
what_it_is: Regulariser that keeps intermediate features of the fine-tuned model informative about a frozen pretrained model's features (variational MI bound). Full text read: DomainBed RN50 avg 65.9 vs ERM 64.2; with SWAD 68.1 vs ERM+SWAD 66.9 (TerraInc 52.9 vs 50.0).
why_it_could_help_us: Soft, always-on version of our PF finding (plain fine-tune erases pretrained deep layers); shown to compose with SWAD on top of the same averaging we use; applies to any encoder (HRNet stage outputs).
cost_to_try: new head or loss (feature regulariser on encoder stages + frozen copy forward)
risk_or_reason_against: Classification evidence; ImageNet features may be a weak anchor for grey-scale EL; one more weight (lambda) to tune.

title: How to Fine-Tune Vision Models with SGD
what_it_is: Abstract: the AdamW > SGD gap in fine-tuning comes from large gradients in the first embedding layer; freezing that layer (<1% params) makes SGD match or beat AdamW on WILDS-FMoW, Camelyon, BREEDS, Waterbirds, DomainNet.
why_it_could_help_us: Gives a cheap PF ablation: keep only the stem frozen (permanently) instead of the whole encoder for 1k steps, and check optimizer choice under distribution shift.
risk_or_reason_against: ViT/ConvNeXt classification; our PF already handles early erasure.

title: Transfer learning in medical image segmentation: New insights from analysis of the dynamics of model parameters and learned representations
what_it_is: Abstract: transfer learning gains are task-dependent and largest for hard tasks with little data; frozen random encoders with trained decoders are quite accurate; feature reuse can be larger in deeper layers.
why_it_could_help_us: Supports PF-style encoder preservation and suggests testing deeper-layer freezing or lower LR for deep stages (layer-wise LR) rather than early layers.
risk_or_reason_against: Medical FCNs, not thin structures; analysis, not a method.

title: SpotTune: Transfer Learning Through Adaptive Fine-Tuning
what_it_is: Per-input policy chooses whether each block uses fine-tuned or frozen pretrained weights (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Learned alternative to a fixed PF freeze.

title: Fine-Tuning can Distort Pretrained Features and Underperform Out-of-Distribution (LP-FT)
what_it_is: Linear-probe then fine-tune.
why_it_could_help_us: PF is a close relative; LP-FT for the decoder-head is the formal variant.

title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
what_it_is: Fine-tune only a subset of layers chosen by shift type.
why_it_could_help_us: Input-level shift (contrast per source) suggests tuning early layers; test vs PF.

title: Masked Images Are Counterfactual Samples for Robust Fine-Tuning
what_it_is: Uses masked images as counterfactual samples during fine-tuning to preserve pretrained robustness (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Another anti-forgetting fine-tune.

title: Channel-wise Knowledge Distillation for Dense Prediction (CWD)
what_it_is: KD loss: softmax-normalise each channel's activation map over space and minimise KL between teacher and student; abstract: PSPNet-R18 +5.81 mIoU on Cityscapes.
why_it_could_help_us: Distil the 5-member PF/C2 ensemble (+ D4 TTA) into one C2 model: the ensemble gave E1 inactive +0.21 (PASS) and crack +0.035 (n.d.); CWD on the crack and inactive logit channels focuses on their most salient locations, which suits sparse classes.
cost_to_try: new head or loss (teacher forward + KD loss)
risk_or_reason_against: Gains reported for small students from large teachers; same-size self/ensemble distillation gains are smaller; teacher errors on E1 transfer.

title: Structured Knowledge Distillation for Dense Prediction
what_it_is: Pixel-wise, pair-wise and holistic (adversarial) KD for dense prediction (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Pair-wise term transfers spatial structure (crack continuity) from ensemble teacher.
risk_or_reason_against: Adversarial term adds instability; aimed at compact students.

title: Knowledge Distillation from a Stronger Teacher (DIST)
what_it_is: Relation-based KD (Pearson correlation of predictions) robust to large teacher-student gaps (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Option if teacher is a foundation-model ensemble much stronger than HRNet-W18.

title: Knowledge distillation with ensembles of convolutional neural networks for medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Distil seed or diverse ensembles into one CNN; TLDR: student keeps ensemble performance.
why_it_could_help_us: Closest-evidence recipe for distilling PF2E into one deployable model.
risk_or_reason_against: Already in MASTER (RUN_NOW, not yet run).

title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
what_it_is: Theory: ensembles of independently trained nets learn different features ('multi-view'); KD and self-distillation can transfer them into one net (TLDR).
why_it_could_help_us: Explains why a 5-seed ensemble can be distilled into one model of the same size without loss.

title: Self-Distillation from the Last Mini-Batch for Consistency Regularization
what_it_is: Uses previous-iteration soft predictions as targets (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Cheap self-distillation without a teacher.

title: Adaptive weighted multi-teacher distillation for efficient medical imaging segmentation with limited data
what_it_is: Multi-teacher KD with adaptive weights for medical segmentation with limited data (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Multi-teacher KD where teachers are our 5 seeds or PF + SKR2 models, weighted per pixel.

title: Semantic segmentation for crack detection via generative knowledge distillation
what_it_is: KD for crack semantic segmentation with generative teacher (abstract preview: aimed at the data-scarcity problem).
why_it_could_help_us: Crack-domain KD evidence.
risk_or_reason_against: Details not read; aimed at lightweight models.

title: Learning from Random Subspace Exploration: Generalized Test-Time Augmentation with Self-supervised Distillation
what_it_is: GTTA: TTA by random subspace perturbations, then self-distil the TTA output into the model (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Distilling our D4 TTA into the network removes 8x inference cost and may regularise.

title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Canonical Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Plain logit KD is competitive in segmentation.
why_it_could_help_us: Use plain KD first before CWD.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Learned attention that combines predictions from several input scales instead of averaging (abstract).
why_it_could_help_us: Upscaled inference (1.5x, 2x) may raise recall of faint 1-2 px cracks on low-contrast CSIR cells; a learned per-pixel scale weighting avoids widening cracks everywhere.
cost_to_try: new head or loss (scale-attention head) or config-only (plain multi-scale TTA)
risk_or_reason_against: Downscaling destroys 1-2 px cracks; 2x input training (Track M) was already tried; 4x compute at 2x scale.

title: Test-time augmentation for deep learning-based cell segmentation on microscopy images
what_it_is: Abstract: flip/rotation TTA with proper merging improves U-Net and Mask R-CNN on DSB 2018 nuclei.
why_it_could_help_us: Confirms D4 TTA choice; merging rule (mean vs max vs vote) is a free knob for recall.

title: Aleatoric uncertainty estimation with test-time augmentation for medical image segmentation with convolutional neural networks
what_it_is: TTA with spatial and intensity transforms as a model of image-based uncertainty; improves segmentation and uncertainty (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Intensity TTA (gamma/contrast) mimics source contrast differences; may help unseen-source recall.
risk_or_reason_against: Intensity TTA may add false cracks on bright gridlines.

title: Learning Loss for Test-Time Augmentation
what_it_is: Small network predicts which augmentations will give low loss for each test input (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Per-cell choice of TTA views for unseen sources.

title: Test-time generative augmentation for medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Generative model produces test-time variants of the input for TTA (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Generated contrast variants as TTA views for unseen sources.
risk_or_reason_against: Heavy; generative edits may invent or erase cracks.

title: Better Aggregation in Test-Time Augmentation
what_it_is: Learned TTA aggregation weights.
why_it_could_help_us: Learned weights for the 8 D4 views.

what_it_is: TTA disagreement as acquisition score for active learning.
why_it_could_help_us: If new modules are labelled, D4 disagreement picks which cells to label first.

title: Local Temperature Scaling for Probability Calibration
what_it_is: Spatially varying temperature predicted per pixel for segmentation calibration (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: A per-pixel temperature could raise low-confidence crack pixels near detected cracks without the global bias shift that tripped the width guard (PF2E/SKR2E).
cost_to_try: new head or loss (small post-hoc net, fitted on CV folds)
risk_or_reason_against: Calibration does not change argmax unless used with a threshold; per-source calibration already tried.

what_it_is: Abstract: equality constraint on logits relative to neighbourhood class proportions (generalises SVLS); better calibration without loss of accuracy.
why_it_could_help_us: Calibrated crack probabilities make the crack-bias choice on CV transfer better to E1.
risk_or_reason_against: SVLS (P066) already covers the idea; on 1-2 px lines neighbourhood proportions are mostly background.

what_it_is: Class-wise penalty weights for calibration learned by augmented Lagrangian (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Rare classes (crack, inactive) need different calibration strength.

title: Average Calibration Losses for Reliable Uncertainty in Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Differentiable marginal L1 average calibration error as auxiliary loss (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Same use as NACL.

title: Confidence Calibration and Predictive Uncertainty Estimation for Deep Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Abstract: compares CE vs Dice loss for segmentation quality and uncertainty, shows ensembling consistently improves calibration of BN + Dice U-Nets, and uses calibrated outputs for quality prediction and OOD detection (brain, heart, prostate).
why_it_could_help_us: Ensembles plus CE give calibrated crack probabilities; useful for thresholding PF2E on CV.

title: Calibrating ensembles for scalable uncertainty quantification in deep learning-based medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Calibration of ensembles for segmentation uncertainty (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Ensemble threshold choice.

title: Improving Calibration and Out-of-Distribution Detection in Deep Models for Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Calibration and OOD detection for medical segmentation trained on small datasets (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Flag cells from unseen layouts (half-cut) before trusting predictions.

title: Thresholding Classifiers to Maximize F1 Score
what_it_is: Abstract: derives the link between best achievable F1 and its threshold; for calibrated probabilities the optimal threshold is half the optimal F1; an uninformative classifier should predict all positive.
why_it_could_help_us: Gives a principled crack threshold: with relF1@2 about 0.87 in-domain but 0.49 on E1, the F1-optimal threshold differs strongly between domains, which explains why biases fitted on CV over- or under-shoot on E1.
risk_or_reason_against: Pixel F1 with 2 px tolerance is not the plain F1 assumed; calibration needed first.

title: Comparative benchmarking of failure detection methods in medical image segmentation: Unveiling the role of confidence aggregation
what_it_is: Benchmark of image-level failure detection for segmentation (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Flag E1-type cells where the model is likely to miss cracks.

title: Segmentation refinement of thin cracks with Minimum Strip Cuts
new_or_pid: NEW (named in D26 gaps, not in MASTER)
what_it_is: Thin-crack mask refinement by minimum strip cuts (title only; no abstract in any index this session either).
why_it_could_help_us: Closest-domain refiner for thin cracks.
risk_or_reason_against: Unreadable this session too; D26's rNCA evidence says one-pass refiners rarely help thin structures.

title: FMS2: Unified Flow Matching for Segmentation and Synthesis of Thin Structures
what_it_is: Training recipe: regress a velocity field from image to mask (flow matching) on a standard U-Net, ODE integration at test time; full text read: 5 crack/vessel sets, 400 train patches each, 256 px; mean IoU 0.511 to 0.599 vs strongest baseline; SynFlow pairs recover near-full performance with 25% labels.
why_it_could_help_us: Architecture-agnostic training objective tested on cracks; could be applied to the C2 network for the crack channel.
risk_or_reason_against: Binary masks only (we have 24 classes); small crack-centred patches; no relF1@2-style tolerant metric; Already PARKED.

what_it_is: Refines boundaries where uncertainty is high in blood-smear microscopy (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Uncertainty-gated refinement for inactive-region edges.
risk_or_reason_against: Blob boundaries, not thin lines; single-author arXiv.

title: ProbCrack-Diff: A structure-aware probabilistic framework for concrete crack segmentation, quantification, and uncertainty estimation
what_it_is: Probabilistic (diffusion) crack segmentation with uncertainty (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Uncertainty maps for crack recall analysis.
risk_or_reason_against: Full generative segmenter, not a recipe.

title: Context- and refinement-driven convolutional architecture for robust crack segmentation under real-world and zero-shot conditions (CrackRefineNet)
what_it_is: Crack architecture with refinement modules evaluated zero-shot (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Zero-shot crack evidence.

what_it_is: Class-agnostic refiner.
why_it_could_help_us: Covered by D26.

what_it_is: Discrete-diffusion refiner.
why_it_could_help_us: Covered by D26 (no Dice gain on DRIVE per rNCA).

title: Boundary loss for highly unbalanced segmentation
what_it_is: Loss = integral of the signed distance map of the GT boundary weighted by predicted foreground probability, added to a regional loss; abstract: significant gains and more stable training on highly unbalanced problems (datasets not read).
why_it_could_help_us: For a 1-2 px crack the signed distance map makes a predicted crack pixel cost proportional to its distance from the nearest GT crack: 1-2 px offsets cost almost nothing (as in relF1@2) while far false cracks (gridlines, crack-free cells) cost most. This aligns the training loss with the tolerant metric.
cost_to_try: new head or loss (precomputed distance maps)
risk_or_reason_against: Designed for blob boundaries; for recall it only rewards GT pixels weakly; needs a ramp-in schedule; JML soft band (tested) is a related tolerance idea.

title: Reducing the Hausdorff Distance in Medical Image Segmentation With Convolutional Neural Networks
what_it_is: Three differentiable HD-type losses (distance transform, morphological, convolution based) (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Penalises isolated far false positives on crack-free cells (guard G2b).
risk_or_reason_against: HD focuses on worst-case outliers, can hurt recall; slow distance transforms per step.

title: Active Boundary Loss for Semantic Segmentation

why_it_could_help_us: Multi-class boundary alignment for inactive regions and busbar edges.

why_it_could_help_us: Inactive-region edges.

what_it_is: Inverse-transformation network measures boundary misalignment as a loss (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Treats small spatial misalignment as a transform rather than errors, close to our 2 px tolerance idea.
cost_to_try: new head or loss (pretrained inverse-transform net)
risk_or_reason_against: Built for object boundaries in Cityscapes; heavy.

title: Regional Hausdorff Distance Losses for Medical Image Segmentation
what_it_is: Regional HD losses (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Variant of HD loss.

what_it_is: Crack topology loss plus frequency-aware network for thin cracks missed due to spectral bias (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: CT-loss is architecture-agnostic and aimed at thin-crack recall.
risk_or_reason_against: Topology losses (clDice, Skeleton Recall) already tested with mixed results.

why_it_could_help_us: Covered by D10/D18.

title: Tversky Loss Function for Image Segmentation Using 3D Fully Convolutional Deep Networks
what_it_is: Tversky index loss with separate FP and FN weights to trade precision for recall; abstract: imbalanced training biases toward high precision / low recall, Tversky improves F2, Dice and PR-AUC on MS lesions (3D).
why_it_could_help_us: E1 crack relR 0.416 vs relP 0.600: a training-time FN weight (beta > alpha) on the crack channel moves the learned operating point toward recall instead of a post-hoc bias.
risk_or_reason_against: A post-hoc crack bias already raised recall but tripped width and false-pixel guards; Tversky may do the same thing at train time.

title: A novel focal tversky loss function with improved attention u-net for lesion segmentation
what_it_is: Focal Tversky: Tversky index raised to 1/gamma so hard, low-overlap examples get more gradient (abstract: better precision/recall trade-off than Dice on small lesions; +25.7% on BUS 2017 and +3.6% on ISIC 2018 vs U-Net, combined with an improved attention U-Net, so the loss effect is not isolated).
why_it_could_help_us: Focal term targets the faint, low-overlap cracks on unseen-source cells that drive the E1 recall gap.
risk_or_reason_against: Same guard risk as Tversky; small 2D lesion sets.

why_it_could_help_us: F-beta loss with beta set to the precision/recall balance we want on crack.

title: sigmoidF1: A Smooth F1 Score Surrogate Loss for Multilabel Classification
what_it_is: Smooth F1 surrogate loss (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: A soft-F1 computed on a 2 px dilated GT/prediction band would be a differentiable relF1@2 surrogate.
risk_or_reason_against: Classification paper; tolerant version is our own construction.

title: Combo loss: Handling input and output imbalance in multi-organ segmentation
what_it_is: Weighted CE (FP/FN weight) + Dice combination (title + index).
why_it_could_help_us: Another FP/FN weighting knob.
risk_or_reason_against: Similar to Dice-12 + weighted CE already tested.

title: A Novel Focal Phi Loss for Power Line Segmentation with Auxiliary Classifier U-Net
what_it_is: Focal loss on the phi (Matthews) coefficient for thin power-line segmentation (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Thin-line, extreme-imbalance precision/recall loss; MCC is less sensitive to the 99.8% background than Dice.

title: The Lovasz-Softmax Loss: A Tractable Surrogate for the Optimization of the Intersection-Over-Union Measure in Neural Networks
what_it_is: Convex IoU surrogate.
why_it_could_help_us: Covered by D18.

title: Unified Focal loss: Generalising Dice and cross entropy-based losses to handle class imbalanced medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Asymmetric focal + focal Tversky compound.
why_it_could_help_us: Covers Tversky family in one loss.

title: Striking the Right Balance: Recall Loss for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: CE weighted by running per-class recall.
why_it_could_help_us: Recall-driven class weights.

title: ResNet strikes back: An improved training procedure in timm
what_it_is: Shows a modern training recipe (longer schedules, strong augmentation, regularisation) changes ResNet-50 results substantially (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Supports a recipe sweep (schedule length, augmentation strength, weight decay, stochastic depth) before architecture changes.

title: How to train your ViT? Data, Augmentation, and Regularization in Vision Transformers
what_it_is: Large study: augmentation and regularisation can substitute for more data (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Small-data argument for stronger augmentation.

title: Smart(Sampling)Augment: Optimal and Efficient Data Augmentation for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: Efficient automated augmentation search for semantic segmentation (abstract preview).
why_it_could_help_us: Search augmentation policy on CV folds (photometric ops that mimic source contrast).
risk_or_reason_against: Small venue; search overfits small CV.

title: MedAugment: Universal automatic data augmentation plug-in for medical image analysis
what_it_is: Automatic augmentation plug-in for medical images, separating pixel and spatial ops (title/index; abstract not shown).
why_it_could_help_us: Ready augmentation policy for grey-scale medical-like images.

title: A parameter-free and effective automatic augmentation method for improved crack segmentation
what_it_is: Parameter-free automatic augmentation for crack segmentation (title only).
why_it_could_help_us: Crack-specific augmentation policy.

title: Cut to the Mix: Simple Data Augmentation Outperforms Elaborate Ones in Limited Organ Segmentation Datasets
what_it_is: CutMix-style augmentation for small segmentation sets.
why_it_could_help_us: Covered by D21.

title: Loss odyssey in medical image segmentation
what_it_is: Benchmark of many segmentation losses (distribution, region, boundary, compound) across medical tasks (title and index; found by snowballing boundary loss; abstract not in index).
why_it_could_help_us: One place to pick which boundary/compound losses held up across tasks before spending GPU time on them.

title: Distance Map Loss Penalty Term for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: CE weighted by a distance map so errors near object boundaries are penalised more (abstract preview; found by snowballing boundary loss).
why_it_could_help_us: Inverse use for us: weight errors by distance from GT crack so 1-2 px offsets are cheap and far false cracks expensive (tolerant-metric aligned).
risk_or_reason_against: Original weighting emphasises boundaries, the opposite of tolerance; our version is a modification.

title: DaWin: Training-free Dynamic Weight Interpolation for Robust Adaptation
what_it_is: Per-sample interpolation coefficient between pretrained and fine-tuned weights chosen from prediction entropy, no training (abstract preview; found by snowballing Model Stock).
why_it_could_help_us: Per-cell interpolation between PF and a more adapted model could help unseen-module cells without hurting in-domain ones.
risk_or_reason_against: CLIP classification; per-sample weights double inference.

title: Structural and Statistical Texture Knowledge Distillation for Semantic Segmentation
what_it_is: KD of low-level texture (structural via contourlet decomposition, statistical) in addition to high-level context (abstract preview; found by snowballing CWD).
why_it_could_help_us: Cracks are low-level texture; distilling low-level features from an ensemble teacher targets exactly the faint-crack detail.
risk_or_reason_against: Aimed at compact students on Cityscapes.

title: Masked Generative Distillation
what_it_is: Student reconstructs teacher features from masked student features (found by snowballing CWD; no abstract in index).
why_it_could_help_us: Feature-level KD option for ensemble-to-single distillation.
